newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall ahead of Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall ahead of Fed meeting.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower on Friday on worries the U.S. Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy on Tuesday.
Traders said the market's movements were exaggerated by very slim trading activity.

"It was very quiet this session," said a trader at a large Argentine bank. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell 0.45 to 117.35, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 declined 3/8 to 82-1/8.
Players said the market has declined gently to a new lower trading range in the last two sessions in anticipation of the policy-setting meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee on Tuesday.
"I think the market has now discounted a 25-basis-point rate hike," said the trader.
Even so the dull, cautious stance adopted by the market in the last couple of sessions may dominate all of next week as well.

Not only is the FOMC meeting likely to keep the market on guard at the beginning of the week, but a 36-hour general strike by Argentine trade unions on Thursday could lead to caution at the end of the week as well.
"The underlying mood is positive, but investors are waiting for a better time to buy," said the trader.

The strike may serve to remind players there is still staunch opposition in much of the country to the government's economic policies and could still threaten the hoped for launch of labor market reforms.
All the same, traders said, the strike will not impact the market directly, but any political statements resulting from it will be watched closely.
In the money markets, one-day call money rates fell to 5.88 percent from 6.28 percent.
